History & Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
27-year-old man evaluated via video minutes after an insect (likely wasp/bee) sting to the right arm; currently shows only a localized cutaneous reaction without objective airway compromise.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Struggling to breathe” and concern for swelling after recent sting.  
• Onset/Timeline: Sting occurred “a few minutes ago” before call; mild subjective dyspnoea and lip tingling started almost immediately; no progression noted during consult.  
• Location: Sting on right arm with small puncture mark and erythematous rash.  
• Associated symptoms: odd tongue sensation, mild right-sided lip soreness; no visible swelling, stridor, chest tightness, wheeze, or generalized urticaria reported/observed.  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: none tried; anxiety acknowledged.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): no dizziness, hypotension, vomiting, abdominal pain, fever, or prior similar reactions.

Past Medical History:
• Eczema (intermittent).  
• Occasional anxiety/panic episodes (never medicated).  
• No previous anaphylaxis; never prescribed adrenaline auto-injector.

Medications:
• None currently.  
Allergies:  
• Penicillin ‑ reaction type not specified.

Social History:
• Occupation: Computer scientist.  
• Lives alone with a pet cat.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: not discussed.

Family History:
• No relevant hereditary illness or allergic/anaphylactic history reported.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: Not recorded.  
General: Speaking full sentences, normal colour, not in distress.  
HEENT: Lips appear normal size; oral cavity and oropharynx normal; no uvular or tongue swelling.  
Respiratory: Breathing unlaboured; no audible stridor or wheeze.  
Cardiovascular: Not assessed.  
Skin: Right arm ‑ small puncture mark with mild erythema/blotchiness; no appreciable swelling, warmth, or tracking erythema.  
Neurological/Abdominal/Musculoskeletal: Not examined.

Investigations:
• None ordered or performed.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Likely uncomplicated localized allergic reaction to a single wasp/bee sting; currently no evidence of systemic anaphylaxis.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Localized allergic reaction – erythema confined to sting site; no systemic signs.  
2. Early IgE-mediated anaphylaxis – timing and subjective dyspnoea/lip tingling raise concern, but objective findings absent.  
3. Anxiety/panic reaction – history of anxiety; subjective breathlessness disproportionate to exam.

Issue 1: Localized reaction to insect sting  
• Plan:  
  – Begin oral antihistamine: Chlorphenamine 4 mg PO, up to 6×/day, or alternative once-daily non-sedating agent (dose/route/frequency per package if chosen).  
  – Cold compress to sting site prn discomfort.

Issue 2: Risk of evolving systemic allergic reaction  
• Plan:  
  – Educated patient on red-flag symptoms: lip/tongue swelling, stridor, worsening dyspnoea, generalized urticaria, dizziness/collapse.  
  – Advise immediate presentation to Emergency Department (dial 999/112) if any such symptoms develop, or lower threshold to re-contact GP.

Issue 3: Possible secondary skin infection (cellulitis)  
• Plan:  
  – Monitor for spreading erythema, increasing pain, warmth, or fever.  
  – If these occur, arrange GP review for possible antibiotics.

General plan items:  
• Provide patient information link on anaphylaxis and sting care.  
• No current need for allergy testing; reconsider if recurrent reactions.  
• No routine follow-up scheduled; patient to book appointment or call if concerns arise.

Quality checks:
• Vitals, smoking/alcohol history, and full medication list not documented in transcript – expected but unavailable.  
• No contradictions between transcript and DDx noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear audio; minimal missing data.
